# 👁 WHAT WAS SEEN — every observation recorded in a code comment

**Generated by `scripts/comment-dict-emit.js` (`npm run dict:rebuild`). Do not hand-edit — regenerate.**

An observation is a comment that records something a seat SAW: a measurement, a verification, a probe result, a reproduction, a
falsification. This index is how one AI learns what another one saw. The authority classes sort comments by what they CLAIM; this
view sorts them by what was SEEN — 1,013 of these are filed as A1-ORDER because they also mention Mark, so no other index shows them as evidence.

**An observation is evidence, never authority.** It was true when it was measured, on that build. A dated one is aged by its date;
an undated one cannot be aged. Re-measure before acting on either — a live sensor or probe outranks a line of text.

## HOW TO WRITE ONE

```
// SEEN <YYYY-MM-DD> (<probe or measurement>): <what was seen, with the number> — knowledge/design/<DOC>.md
```

- the **date** ages it · the **method** (a probe name, a counter, a screenshot) makes it re-derivable · the **number** makes it checkable
- the **doc link** files it in `KNOWLEDGE-LINKS.md`; put screenshots in `knowledge/design/shots/` and research probes in
  `knowledge/design/probes/`, linked from the doc
- no rule words and no names in an observation (NEVER, DO NOT, LAW, BANNED, MANDATE, BINDING, "by default", Mark): it describes what
  was seen, and the comment gate reads those words as rule claims
